newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPALS -- quiet, gains 1/4 to 3/8 point.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPALS -- quiet, gains 1/4 to 3/8 point.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices gained 1/4 to 3/8 point Monday, aided by a light calendar, a rising Treasury market and good follow-through action from Friday, traders said.
Activity was extremely quiet, and traders reported seeing very little institutional selling.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was up 11/32 at 98-3/32 to yield 6.52 percent.
With little scheduled in the way of new data Monday, government traders said the market was rangebound ahead of Tuesday's new economic indicators and the Federal Open Market Committee meeting.
The Fed is widely expected to hold interest rates steady, especially given Friday's dramatic stock market sell-off.
Tuesday's data includes housing starts for July at 0830 EDT. Economists surveyed by Reuters said they expect the figure to be 1.46 million, compared to 1.452 million in June.

In debt futures, the September municipal contract gained 14/32 at 120-5/32, while September T-bonds were 15/32 higher at 114-3/32. The MOB spread narrowed to 194 ticks from 195 at the close on Friday.

In the muni secondary, bids on Denver Airport MBIA 5-1/4s of 2017 were unchanged at 5.45 percent. Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority 5.0s of 2024 were eight basis points lower, at 5.47 percent.
Tuesday's new issues were expected to total $474 million in 31 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings totalled $235 million in 12 sales, with a $46 million Texas Housing Agency offering through John Nuveen & Co., Inc. topping the list.
On the competitive side, 19 sales totaling $239 million were scheduled. A $62 million Fort Bend Independent School District, Texas, offering was the largest.
For the entire week, a total of $1.9 billion in 105 offerings are slated, including a $200 million St. Louis, Mo., deal through Bear Stearns & Co.
